item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-23

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-23 04:29 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity but heavily bug-burdened maintenance phase. In the last 24 hours, 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated, with a near-even split between open and closed items (issues: 290 open / 210 closed; PRs: 279 open / 221 merged or closed). The activity pattern is overwhelmingly dominated by regression triage and startup/recovery stability work tied to the 2026.9.x line, alongside a single patch release (v2026.10.6) driven by an upstream Node.js security dependency. The project shows strong contributor throughput (many fresh PRs from maintainer steipete and the roboclaw-bot automation), but the density of P0/P1 crash-loop, message-loss, and session-state bugs — several open for weeks — signals that stability debt is outpacing feature delivery. Overall health: active and responsive, but strained on reliability.

2. Releases

v2026.10.6 (1 new release)

  • Patched Node runtime required (breaking/environmental): OpenClaw now requires Node 24.22.1+ on the 24 line, or 26.12.1+ on the 26 line. These versions reject TLS chains signed with the compromised certificate keys addressed in the October 2026 Node.js security releases.
  • Migration notes: Operators on older Node 24.x/26.x builds must upgrade their runtime before/alongside this release, or TLS connections may fail. Docker images already ship Node 24.2x (truncated in release notes).
  • Action item: Self-hosted and CI environments pinned to older Node minors should verify their runtime version to avoid silent TLS rejection.

3. Project Progress

221 PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h. Notable themes among closed/carried-forward work:

  • UI/perf modernization (Solid migration): A large cluster of maintainer PRs from steipete and roboclaw-bot advances the Control UI refactor — lazy-loading gateway switch confirmation (#181302), deferring background content (#181306), and gzip boot transfer reductions (#181233: startup -12,527 B, Chat -52,342 B, New Session -32,092 B).
  • Gateway startup fix: #181289 (steipete) allows plugin loading to proceed before orphan marking finishes on large session stores — directly targeting the slow-startup complaint class.
  • Recovery/readiness fix: #181274 (closed) fixed a recovery fixture hanging Gateway readiness after saved chat input replay.
  • Secret handling hardening: #167250 prevents malformed UTF-8 from overwriting stored secrets (security-sensitive, awaiting maintainer).

Closed bugs include several long-standing items: Discord mention-gating (#44502), macOS memory detection skip (#47273), and Tailscale Serve claim loss (#148308).

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume:

  1. #160959 — P0, 42 comments: Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression). The single hottest thread; 🦞 diamond lobster rating. Need: event-loop yielding during plugin generation capture.
  2. #42475 — P2, 27 comments: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway. Long-running (since March), still needs product decision. Need: operator cost guardrails without external monitoring.
  3. #11829 — CLOSED, 21 comments: Security roadmap to protect API keys from agent access. Need: layered secret isolation from LLM context.
  4. #157531 — 17 comments: The 2026.9.7 Fixes Tracker, coordinating 18/21 established P1 candidates. Signal: maintainers are batching release hardening.
  5. #140010 — P1, 14 comments: Windows sleep/resume WebSocket reconnect failures (30–60s+). Need: thaw-recovery prioritization ahead of busy gateway.

Underlying pattern: the community's energy is concentrated on startup/event-loop stalls, cost governance, and secret protection, not on new capabilities.

5. Bugs & Stability

Severity-ranked open items updated today (no dedicated fix PR explicitly linked unless noted):

P0 — Crash/loss class:

  • #160959: Gateway blocks minutes on large plugin capture — startup regression.
  • #156712: openclaw triage repair subprocess won't exit, holds gateway-lifecycle lock, blocks restart.
  • #156674: macOS gateway resource pressure with long-lived Codex workers.
  • #158592: Post sleep/wake, model runtime publication times out permanently — every inbound message fails until restart.
  • #166634: Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash recovery.
  • #141615: WebChat "Authenticated profile verification unavailable" wedges all RPCs.
  • #166004: Windows scheduled-task Gateway won't start; 2026.9.8 update rolls back.
  • #141413: macOS app omits token for local Gateway using SecretRef.

P1:

  • #172837: Codex nativeSubagentAssignments never removed — re-pinned/re-sent per parent thread (message-loss).
  • #167557: Plugin data/settings migration never converges (Linux/npm).
  • #180690: doctor --fix heap OOM at 6 GB on ~810-agent state; ~110 min across 3 passes.
  • #138042: Gateway control requests stall 157–276s.
  • #160485: Windows plugin load CPU-bound; 3 channel plugins = 57.4s of 60s phase.
  • #145690, #154716, #159787, #155359.

Theme: A recurring sleep/wake + event-loop stall + session-state cluster (Windows and macOS) is the dominant stability risk. Only #181289/#181274 have adjacent fix PRs today; most P0s lack a linked fix PR.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #42475 Per-agent cost budgets — high engagement, needs product decision; plausible candidate for an upcoming release given cost-control demand.
  • #53763 Built-in headless browser (now CLOSED, 18 comments) — reduced fragility for web access.
  • #15032 Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents (CLOSED) — prompt-injection defense; strong security alignment.
  • #138279 Linux aarch64 companion builds (deb + AppImage).
  • #144306 Automation delivery to paired nodes (notifications).
  • #71330 Configurable memory promotion target (CLOSED) and #87660 lifecycle-aware MEMORY.md curation — memory subsystem is a growing roadmap area.

Prediction: cost budgets (#42475) and sub-agent tool sandboxing (#15032) are the most likely to land in the next minor, given security/cost framing and maintainer attention.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain points: Startups and post-wake recovery are the top frustration — #160959, #140010, #158592, #157812 all describe multi-second-to-minute unreachability after sleep or update. Windows operators are disproportionately affected (updates, scheduled tasks, plugin load).
  • UX friction: Mobile keyboard occlusion (#137508), WebChat duplicated assistant text (#140723), stale context-window widget (#165421).
  • Security sensitivity: Internal runtime-context carrier leaking as visible turns across Teams (#136360), Slack/Telegram/Feishu/Discord — a cross-channel systemic concern.
  • Dissatisfaction signal: #151112 — self-hosted operators feel entangled in secret/approval loops, reducing autonomy.
  • Satisfaction signal: High-thumbs items (e.g., sandbox bug #43996 with 👍:2, memory curation #87660 with 👍:2) indicate users actively validating fixes.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or maintainer-blocked items warranting attention:

  • #42475 (since 2026-03-10): Per-agent cost budgets — 7+ months, needs product decision.
  • #138042 (since 2026-09-04): Gateway control stalls 157–276s — no fix PR, P1.
  • #138279 (since 2026-09-04): Linux aarch64 builds — stalled on product decision.
  • #126836 (since 2026-08-20): sessions.reset returns ok but creates no window — silently swallowed sessions.
  • #167250 (since 2026-10-08): Secret-overwrite hardening PR — security review pending.
  • #180690 (new, P1): doctor --fix OOM on large state — high operational impact for power users, no linked PR yet.

Maintainer recommendation: Prioritize a coordinated "wake/stall recovery" epic (spanning #140010, #158592, #138042, #160959) and unblock the two security reviews (#167250, plus the SecretRef macOS bug #141413) to reduce the P0 backlog before the next feature release.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report

Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Analysis Date: 2026-10-23 | Sources: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape in late 2026 is high-velocity, security-hardening, and transitioning from single-agent assistants to distributed, multi-owner agent platforms. Across all five projects, intake of issues and PRs substantially outpaces merge throughput, indicating a market where user ambition (federation, remote execution, memory governance) is running ahead of maintainer bandwidth. A common maturation arc is visible: every project except the dormant IronClaw is in an active stability/security hardening phase — patching sleep/wake recovery, credential isolation, approval-model gaps, and supply-chain integrity rather than shipping headline features. Community discourse is converging on trust, control, and interoperability — least-privilege enforcement, memory/cost governance, and cross-gateway collaboration — rather than raw capability. Meanwhile, platform-specific reliability debt (especially Windows) and documented-but-unenforced security controls are the ecosystem's most recurring dissatisfaction signals.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues Updated (24h) PRs Updated (24h) Merge/Close Throughput Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw 500 (290 open / 210 closed) 500 (279 open / 221 merged/closed) High (~221/day) v2026.10.6 (Node TLS security patch) 🟡 Active but reliability-strained
Hermes Agent 50 (49 open / 1 closed) 50 (41 open / 9 closed) Low (9/50, mostly old backlog) None 🟠 Very high activity, backlog growing
IronClaw 2 (1 open / 1 closed) 6 (5 open / 1 closed) Minimal (Dependabot only) None 🟢 Quiet / maintenance mode
QwenPaw 22 (20 open / 2 closed) 50 (48 open / 2 merged) Low (2/50, release-cut freeze) v2.2.2.post1 (security patch) 🟢 Strong responsiveness, review bottleneck
ZeroClaw 35 50 (42 open / 8 closed) Zero merged None (pre-v0.9.0 freeze) 🟡 Disciplined stabilization, merge-queue gated

Legend: Health Score weights activity, throughput, stability, security posture, and backlog risk. Key observation: Only OpenClaw demonstrates high merge throughput; Zeroclaw and QwenPaw are functionally frozen (release gate / review backlog); Hermes has intake ≫ resolution; IronClaw is inert.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs Peers

  • Scale & responsiveness: With ~500 issues + ~500 PRs touched in 24h and ~221 PRs merged, OpenClaw operates at an order of magnitude greater throughput than any peer. It is the de facto reference implementation of the ecosystem.
  • Infrastructure maturity: Only project with active release cadence (v2026.10.6), Docker images, cross-platform companions, and formal triage automation (roboclaw-bot).
  • Broadest channel and platform surface: Covers Discord, Slack, Telegram, Feishu, Teams, WebChat, plus Windows/macOS/Linux companions.

Technical Approach Differences

  • Gateway-centric architecture: A single long-lived gateway process brokers sessions, plugins, and channels — powerful but the root cause of its dominant failure class (event-loop stalls, plugin capture blocking for minutes, sleep/wake reconnect failures). Peers like ZeroClaw are explicitly moving away from mandatory gateways (CLI-only builds, PR #11975).
  • Plugin model is heavyweight: Large external plugin capture is the P0 hot topic (#160959), whereas QwenPaw is refactoring channels into subprocess-isolated plugins (PR #8187) and ZeroClaw treats plugins as installable release artifacts.

Community Size Comparison

Dimension OpenClaw Peers
Daily issue/PR churn ~1000 events 8–100 events
Top thread engagement 42 comments (P0) 40 (Hermes), 15 (ZeroClaw), 7 (QwenPaw), 0 (IronClaw)
Reaction signal Moderate Hermes leads (42 👍 on #18715)
Contributor breadth Maintainer + automation dominant Hermes/QwenPaw show more first-time contributors

Verdict: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's center of gravity and de facto standard, but its stability debt (many P0 crash-loop/session-state bugs open for weeks without fix PRs) is the ecosystem's largest single risk. Its breadth is a moat; its reliability is its exposure.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

The following requirements emerge independently across multiple projects, signaling genuine ecosystem-wide demand:

Cross-Cutting Need Projects Specific Evidence
Multi-agent / cross-gateway collaboration OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw Hermes #97681 (federated bots) + #18715 (remote agent/local tools, 42 👍); OpenClaw sub-agent tool sandboxing #15032; ZeroClaw delegate allowlist #8279
Least-privilege & enforced tool restrictions OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw OpenClaw #15032; Hermes approval-gate expansion #142834; ZeroClaw #8279 (allowlist bypass), #11989 (excluded_tools ignored)
Approval-model maturity beyond shell/code Hermes, OpenClaw, ZeroClaw Hermes #141346 (osascript data loss), #142834; OpenClaw secret/approval friction #151112; ZeroClaw SOP authority escalation
Memory governance (budget + write-time acceptance) OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw OpenClaw #87660 lifecycle-aware MEMORY.md; Hermes #135039 budget/acceptance; QwenPaw memory context PR #8376
Cost guardrails / per-agent budgets OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw OpenClaw #42475 (7+ months open); Hermes #135039 (turn-injection cost); QwenPaw media replay runaway #8335
Credential / secret isolation OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, Hermes OpenClaw #11829 (API keys from agent context); ZeroClaw OIDC credential encoding #11957; Hermes supply-chain SHA256 pins
Session lifecycle correctness (resume / cold-load / cancel) OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw OpenClaw #126836 (silent session loss); Hermes #139796 (cold resume not_found), #136713; ZeroClaw session store #11898
Platform portability (Windows, ARM64) OpenClaw, Hermes, IronClaw, QwenPaw Windows dominates OpenClaw/Hermes bugs; IronClaw ARM64 #3168; QwenPaw Windows CRLF/GBK PRs #8234/#8235
Supply-chain / release-artifact integrity OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw OpenClaw Node TLS patch; Hermes Electron/TTS checksums; ZeroClaw Discord release-binary proof #10999; QwenPaw emSign CA fix

Signal: The ecosystem is collectively discovering that autonomy must be paired with enforceable policy, and policy must be verifiable in shipped artifacts. This is the defining requirement wave of 2026-10.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Interpretation:

  • OpenClaw and Hermes compete on breadth and ambition — the generalist platforms.
  • ZeroClaw is the security-specialist — it treats least-privilege and provable releases as first-class, and its issue quality (allowlist bypasses, SOP escalation) reflects a security-literate community.
  • QwenPaw is the extensibility play — Hub-based team operations plus a plugin ecosystem refactor aimed at v2.3.0.
  • IronClaw is the evaluation/research outlier — Rust/WASM performance focus, currently idle.
  • Hermes is the federation visionary — cross-gateway collaboration and split compute/execution are its signature bets.

For a decision-maker, this means the reliability of a project is better predicted by process discipline than by commit velocity.

7. Trend Signals

Industry Trends Extracted from Community Feedback

1. From "assistant" to "fleet/federation." The single strongest future signal is Hermes' #97681 (cross-gateway collaboration, 40 comments) and #18715 (remote agent + local tools, 42 👍), echoed by OpenClaw sub-agent sandboxing and ZeroClaw delegation. Developers should architect for inter-agent identity, trust boundaries, and message routing now, because single-agent designs will hit federation walls within the next release cycle.

2. Policy is the new security perimeter — and it's currently under-specified. Every security-mature project is fighting "documented controls that don't enforce": ZeroClaw's excluded_tools ignored, delegate allowlist bypass, SOP authority gaps; OpenClaw's secret exposure; Hermes' osascript auto-approval data loss. Developers building on this ecosystem must assume tool/skill sandboxing is a liability, not a guarantee, and should prefer architectures with explicit, testable policy enforcement (ZeroClaw's approach is the model to watch).

3. Approval models must understand consequence, not just command type. The Hermes #141346 incident (smart approval closing unsaved PowerPoint, deleting exports) is the clearest signal that current shell/code-execution approval heuristics are insufficient. The next wave of agent safety will be semantic/destructive-action-aware — a substantial greenfield opportunity for tooling vendors.

4. Memory is becoming a governed resource, not just a store. OpenClaw, Hermes, and QwenPaw are all independently building memory budgets, acceptance gates, and lifecycle curation. Per-turn memory injection cost/latency (#135039) and privacy overreach (#116788) are forcing write-time policy. Memory subsystems are transitioning from "feature" to "cost/privacy surface" requiring governance.

5. Reliability ≠ stability across platforms — Windows is the ecosystem's weak flank. Windows update failures, permission mismatches, plugin CPU stalls, and kanban deadlocks dominate Hermes and OpenClaw bug reports. Cross-platform testing (especially Windows and ARM64) is a durable competitive differentiator and an underserved gap across all projects.

6. Release-artifact trust is a first-class user concern. ZeroClaw's demand to "prove Discord plugin installs from a published binary," QwenPaw's emSign/CA remediation, and Hermes' checksum pins show users now verify what actually shipped, not just what passed CI. Reproducible, verifiable releases are moving from best practice to baseline expectation.

7. The merge/review pipeline — not contributor supply — is the ecosystem's binding constraint. Four of five active projects show open-PR counts 5–24× their daily merge rate. For maintainers, review bandwidth (not development) is the growth limiter; for contributors, this means PR success increasingly depends on aligning with release gates and maintainer priorities.

Bottom Line for Technical Decision-Makers

  • For production deployments today: OpenClaw offers the most capability and channels but carries the highest reliability/security-review risk; ZeroClaw offers the strongest safety posture but is pre-v0.9.0; QwenPaw offers the best release discipline and extensibility roadmap.
  • For platform builders: Bet on federation primitives, enforceable policy engines, and governed memory — these are the three unmet needs every project is independently confirming.
  • For contributors/investors: The ecosystem's bottleneck is maintainer review throughput and cross-platform reliability, not ideas. Projects that solve review scaling and Windows/ARM parity will convert community energy into shipped value fastest.
  • Watch items: Hermes' federation decisions (#97681, #18715), ZeroClaw's v0.9.0 authority stack and the unmitigated #8279/S0 bypass, and OpenClaw's wake/stall recovery epic — these will shape the ecosystem's next quarter more than any new feature.

  • Plugin refactor for a lighter, more modular core.
  • Preliminary test results shared; maintainers actively soliciting community needs.

Likely candidates for v2.3.0 or soon after:

  • Global Skill & MCP management in Hub (#8275) — strong team-use case, low architectural risk, 1 👍. Fits the Hub multi-user trajectory.
  • Plugin theme extension points (#8071) — highest-commented feature issue; natural companion to the plugin refactor.
  • Channel plugin extraction (#8187) — already in PR form, size/XXXL.
  • Desktop scroll-lock toggle (#7339) — open since August, simple ask, steady interest.

Prediction: v2.3.0 is shaping up as the "extensibility release" — plugin isolation, theme hooks, and Hub-shared configuration are the coherent theme. Security patches (2.2.2.post1) are a stabilizing precursor.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points voiced:

  1. Upgrade fragility — Multiple users (#8388, #8378) report channels/models breaking after upgrading. The _qwenpaw_remote_backend missing-module error is particularly damaging because it makes the agent believe its own environment is corrupt, producing confusing self-diagnosis output. Upgrade paths need verification testing.
  2. Silent failures — DingTalk (#8343), Telegram (#8329), and the quote-routing issue (#8342) all share a pattern: the agent appears to work but the user never receives a reply or loses context. Silent data/context loss is worse than loud errors.
  3. Team/Hub friction — #8275 and #8392 (closed) both stem from Hub being used in real multi-user teams, where per-user config duplication and local-model display quirks surface.
  4. Contributor friction — #8377 shows a clean checkout fails pytest collection, contradicting CONTRIBUTING.md and potentially deterring first-time contributors (ironic given the healthy number of first-time-contributor PRs today).

Satisfaction signals: The v2.3.0 roadmap issue (#8289) drew positive engagement (1 👍, substantive comments) and the security response was fast and transparent. Users are invested enough to file detailed, evidence-rich bug reports — a sign of an engaged community rather than churn.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention — long-open, high-impact, or lacking a fix owner:

Item Age Why it matters Link
#7339 Desktop scroll-lock toggle ~2 months (since 2026-08-27) Simple, well-scoped UX ask; still no PR. Low-hanging fruit for goodwill. Link
#8078 Cross-session messages split into separate chats ~3 weeks (since 2026-10-02) Core/backend + Console data-model issue; conversation fragmentation affects trust in history. Link
#8071 Plugin theme extension point ~3 weeks, 7 comments Most-discussed feature issue; ties into the v2.3.0 plugin work but has no linked PR. Link
#8350 Feishu blocks main loop 2 days Severe, but no fix PR yet — deserves an owner given the SIGTERM-exit hazard. Link
#8343 DingTalk silent reply drop 3 days Reproduced on main; no fix PR yet. Link
#8268 Bounded run-completion callback 1 week (PR) Fixes half of #8173 (runs stuck running forever); needs review to land. Link
#8244 Skip disabled channel SDKs at startup ~9 days 15.1s startup stall on default Windows profile — real perf win, marked "Under Review." Link
#8236 Ollama num_ctx sizing ~9 days Affects all local Ollama users' context behavior; no review activity noted. Link

Backlog health assessment: The open-PR count (48) versus merged/closed (2) today is a significant review bottleneck. Several fix PRs (#8268, #8244, #8236, #8303, #8299) have been open 1–9 days with no merge. If this persists, contributor momentum — currently healthy with multiple first-time contributors — could erode. Recommend maintainers triage the "Under Review" and size/S/size/M fix PRs to sustain velocity alongside the v2.3.0 refactor.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in an intense pre-v0.9.0 stabilization cycle. Activity remains very high (35 issues touched, 50 PRs updated in 24h) but is dominated by bug-fixing, security hardening, and release-gate work rather than new features. Notably, no PRs were merged and no releases were cut today — only 8 PRs were closed/merged in the window, against 42 still open, suggesting a review bottleneck or a deliberate freeze ahead of v0.9.0. A cluster of P1/P0 security issues (delegate allowlist bypass, SOP authority escalation, principal-scope leaks) are under active repair via stacked PRs from distinguished contributor IftekharUddin. Overall project health looks cautious but disciplined: the team is closing regressions (OIDC JWKS race, daemon session store) while opening release-blocking tickets (TLS WebSocket upgrade, OIDC enrollment encoding) — classic late-stage stabilization.

2. Releases

No new releases today. The most recent shipped artifact referenced in the backlog is v0.8.6, with v0.8.7 tickets (plugins, email, CI) closing out and v0.9.0 tickets accruing. Maintainers should note two v0.8.6 shipping concerns still in play:

  • #11828 (closed) — arm64 dist image OOM in docker-publish.yml; v0.8.6 may have shipped without its dist image.
  • #10999 (open, blocked) — Discord plugin install from release binary verified on v0.8.6, but full proof still pending.

No changelog or migration notes are available for an unreleased 0.9.0.

3. Project Progress

With zero PRs merged today, progress is best read as "repairs staged, not landed." The active merge queue is heavily stacked:

  • Identity/authority hardening (P0–P1), IftekharUddin's stack: #11225 (preserve owner in delegation, P0) → #11230 (withhold session-data tools from non-admins) → #11220 (require admin authority for SOP execution) → #11234 (judge queued session ownership by current authority).
  • Durable rename recovery: #11301 — shared committed-rename recovery across CLI, gateway, and RPC (XL, needs-author-action).
  • ZeroClaw without a gateway: #11269 (stop metrics/embedded-web enabling the gateway), #11975 (CLI-only build UX), directly addressing #11969 and #11971.
  • Channel correctness: #11990 fixes the "excluded_tools is never applied" bug (#11989); #11651 adds Telegram 429 flood-gating.

Closed issues today included several v0.8.7 regressions: #10558 (Cranelift CI timeout), #11357 (plugin remove path deletion), #11327 (plugin tool-name pre-emption), #11898 (daemon session store on fresh data dir), and #11902 (OIDC JWKS race). Nothing merged means every fix above is still in flight.

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #7432 — Tracker: runtime, dashboard sign-in, gateway delivery (P2, release:v0.9.0) 15 The umbrella roadmap issue for v0.9.0; everything below hangs off it.
2 #10526 CLOSED — RFC: append-only session events & deterministic replay 13 Architecture RFC; closed suggests direction accepted, but no implementing PR is visible.
3 #10999 — Prove Discord plugin install from release binary 9 Release-verification rigor; real network proof on macOS arm64.
4 #8279 — Delegate bypasses parent tool allowlist (P1, S0) 5 Longest-running security hole (opened June, still open, updated today).

Underlying needs: the community is converging on three demands — (a) provable release artifacts (plugins must be installable from a published binary, not just in-tree), (b) principled session/state semantics (event sourcing, deterministic replay, survivor sessions), and (c) enforceable least-privilege (delegate, SOP, channel-scoped tools). The tracker #7432 is functioning as an informal release spec.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by declared severity and exploitability:

S0 / P1 — Security-critical

  • #8279 — delegate filters the unfiltered parent tool set, so a sub-agent can invoke tools the parent policy excludes. No linked fix PR found. This is the highest-risk open item and has been open ~4 months.
  • #11225 (P0) — memory delegation loses principal scope; fix staged.

S1 — Workflow blocked

  • #11957 — OIDC enrollment sends raw client credentials in Basic header, breaking client_credentials/device-grant when secrets contain reserved chars (RFC 6749 §2.3.1 violation). Fix exists: #11968.

S2 — Degraded

  • #11951 — Gateway WebSocket upgrades fail over built-in TLS (101 then close), breaking dashboard chat. Release-blocking for v0.9.0; no fix PR yet.
  • #11962 — 64 live RPC sessions never released when idle → remote clients can exhaust them. Fix staged: #11964.
  • #11823 — shell scanner skips command substitution inside unquoted-delimiter heredocs (sandbox escape vector). No fix PR.
  • #11991 — outbound email HTML passes raw markup and arbitrary image URLs from agent text (phishing/tracking risk).
  • #11989 — per-channel excluded_tools silently ignored. Fix staged: #11990.
  • #11970 — agents delete/rename skip owned-state cascade in gateway-less builds.

S3 — Minor

  • #11972 — gateway get-paircode exits 0 on failure (scripts can't detect it). #11987 — inline nosemgrep comments don't suppress code-scanning alerts. #11969 — metrics/embedded-web features pull in the whole gateway.

Stability verdict: regression inflow is balanced by staged fixes, but #8279 and #11951 are unmitigated and both are security/release blockers.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Clear v0.9.0 candidates, in rough priority order:

  1. Dashboard OIDC sign-in — #11961 / PR #11965, plus follow-ons #11984 (non-admin scoped chat) and #11985 (JWKS/failed-write/retirement tests). All tagged release:v0.9.0.
  2. CLI-only source build — #11971 + #11969, fixes in #11975/#11269. Strong "minimal server install" demand.
  3. Channel sender-role narrowing — #11068 ([peer_groups.<name>] risk_profile) — a policy-language feature, XL, security-tagged.
  4. Email channel polish — operator templates + sanitized HTML (#11992), quoted replies (#11939).
  5. Shell policy explainability — #11799 → PR #11983: refusals carry a reason + operator hint.
  6. XMPP/Prosody channel with optional OMEMO — #11847, XL, community-contributed.

Prediction: v0.9.0 ships OIDC dashboard sign-in, CLI-only build, and the identity/authority hardening stack. Sender-role narrowing and XMPP are more likely v0.9.x.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Release trust is the loudest theme. #10999 shows users want to install published plugins and have it verified end-to-end, not just pass in CI. #11828 (dist image OOM) reinforces that the release pipeline is the weak link.
  • Security posture is being pressure-tested. Multiple independent reporters (IftekharUddin, wangmiao0668000666, mov-xound-glitch) found allowlist bypasses, SOP privilege escalation, and unescaped email HTML. This reads as engaged, security-literate users finding real gaps — healthy scrutiny, but a warning that the trust model is under-specified.
  • Least-privilege is expected by default. #11989 (excluded_tools documented but silently ignored) is a classic "docs promise, code doesn't deliver" frustration; #8279 is the same class at higher stakes.
  • Operator UX matters. #11799 (refusals should say why) and #11972 (exit 0 on failure) are small but high-annoyance defects for anyone scripting ZeroClaw.
  • Pain point pattern: documented security controls that don't actually enforce. This is the single most recurring dissatisfaction signal today.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, ranked by risk × staleness:

Item Age Why it needs attention
#8279 — delegate allowlist bypass (S0/P1) ~4 months Highest-severity open issue, no fix PR. Every day it's open is a policy-bypass window.
#11301 — durable rename recovery (XL, needs-author-action) 3 weeks Blocked on author; rename failures strand agent state.
#11068 — channel turns by sender role (XL, needs-author-action) 1 month A whole policy dimension waiting on review.
#11234 — queued session ownership (needs-maintainer-review) ~3.5 weeks Sitting in maintainer queue; part of the P1 authority stack.
#11651 — Telegram 429 handling (needs-author-action, XL) 13 days Rate-limit storm affects every Telegram deployment.
#11847 — XMPP channel (XL) 4 days Large community contribution; risks bit-rot if unreviewed.

Bottom line for maintainers: the merge queue is the bottleneck. Forty-two open PRs, several stacked and several tagged needs-author-action or needs-maintainer-review, are gating v0.9.0 — while two unmitigated security/release blockers (#8279, #11951) sit outside that queue entirely. Prioritizing review throughput and assigning owners to those two issues would do more for project health than any new feature this week.

item.content:encoded:
Bản tin hạ tầng AI 2026-10-23

Tạo lúc: 2026-10-23 04:29 UTC | Dự án theo dõi: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

So sánh chéo dự án

Báo cáo Hạ tầng AI Liên dự án — 2026-10-23

1. Tổng quan Hệ sinh thái

Ngăn xếp hạ tầng AI đang ở pha ưu tiên tính đúng đắn hơn tính năng: trên cả sáu dự án, các lỗi hồi quy nghiêm trọng về độ ổn định (ô nhiễm KV âm thầm, xâm phạm chuỗi cung ứng, kernel kích hoạt sai) chiếm ưu thế trong tracker so với các thông báo model mới. Hỗ trợ model tiên phong đã hội tụ quanh một tập nhỏ kiến trúc — DeepSeek-V4.x, Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.x, Nemotron 3.5 — và cuộc đua cạnh tranh giờ xoay quanh độ phủ checkpoint ngày-0 theo từng tầng phần cứng thay vì các lớp model hoàn toàn mới. Đa dạng hóa phần cứng là thật nhưng không đồng đều: NVIDIA Blackwell/SM120/GB300 và AMD ROCm/MI355X chi phối công việc hiệu năng, trong khi Ampere (SM8x) và Intel SYCL ngày càng trở thành công dân hạng hai trên các checkpoint mới nhất. Ở tầng gateway và huấn luyện, câu chuyện là quản lý rủi ro — sự cố chuỗi cung ứng 1.107.0 của LiteLLM và sự cố kéo dài của Ollama Cloud Pro là lời nhắc rằng phần "nhàm chán" ở giữa ngăn xếp lại mang bán kính ảnh hưởng vượt trội. Trong khi đó, các bề mặt workflow/soạn tác nhân (Unsloth Flows, SGLang diffusion, llama.cpp realtime audio) đang mở rộng, đẩy các serving engine sang lãnh thổ nền tảng ứng dụng.

2. So sánh Hoạt động

Dự án Tầng Issue mở được nhấn mạnh PR được nhấn mạnh Trạng thái phát hành (24h) Tín hiệu chi phối
vLLM Serving engine ~7 (gồm 2 lỗi ô nhiễm âm thầm) ~10+ Không DSv4.1 graph capture + tính đúng đắn PD-KV
SGLang Serving engine ~10 (gồm crash scheduler) ~8 Không Tính đúng đắn GLM/Kimi + host-sync diffusion
llama.cpp Runtime cục bộ ~8 ~10 7 bản phát hành (b11815–b11829) Hiệu năng SYCL + lỗi long-context
Ollama Runtime cục bộ + cloud ~10 ~5 Không Sự cố cloud + hồi quy Windows
LiteLLM Gateway ~20+ ~10 Không (yank, không phát hành) Xâm phạm chuỗi cung ứng
Unsloth Nền tảng fine-tuning ~9 ~7 Không Trình soạn node Flows + GGUF đa node

Ghi chú: số lượng chỉ phản ánh các mục được digest nhấn mạnh, không phải tracker đầy đủ. llama.cpp là dự án duy nhất có nhịp phát hành đều; "không phát hành" của LiteLLM là một lệnh yank, không phải ngày yên ắng.

3. Cuộc đua Hỗ trợ Model

Độ phủ model tiên phong đang hội tụ, nhưng độ phủ theo tầng phần cứng phân kỳ mạnh.

Model / Arch vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
DeepSeek-V4.1 / V4-Flash ✅ (SM100 trước; SM8x đang chờ #50576) ✅ (ROCm prefill CP #43465) ⚠️ DSv4.1-Flash-1017 load fail #14695 ❌ ⚠️ sidecar fix #14431
Kimi-K3 — ✅ (kèm lưu ý: GB300 #45367, SM90 #45755) — ❌ ❌
GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM5 — ✅ (hiệu năng SM90 #45373, SM120 #42012) ✅ (tùy chọn input GLM5) ⚠️ thoái hóa cloud #18980 ❌
Qwen3.8 / Qwen4exp ✅ (ROCm MI355X) — ✅ (DFlash, loại bỏ kq_mask #30965) ✅ (chỉ cloud) ❌
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt — — ✅ (GQA/tokenizer #23343) ✅ (MLX 74B-A9B #19229) ❌
MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 / MOSS-Image — ✅ SANA-Sprint ✅ MiniCPM-OCR ❌ ✅ MOSS-Image
Muse Spark ✅ (ROCm MoE #63263) ✅ (Ngày-0 #44664–67) ❌ ❌ ❌

Ai đang dẫn đầu: vLLM và SGLang là các engine tiên phong ngày-0, nhưng cả hai đều giới hạn các checkpoint DeepSeek mới nhất sau SM90+/Blackwell — bỏ rơi A100/A800 và Ampere tiêu dùng. llama.cpp có độ rộng hỗ trợ model lớn nhất (Nemotron, GLM5, MiniCPM, MOSS) nhưng chậm chân ở dòng DeepSeek mới nhất. Ollama dẫn đầu về đóng gói MLX/Nemotron cắm-là-chạy cho Mac và DGX Spark. Unsloth là ngoại lệ: tập trung vào multimodal + GGUF + đa node thay vì độ phủ LLM tiên phong thuần túy.

4. Biên giới Hiệu năng

Nỗ lực tối ưu tập trung vào năm nhóm, với chuyên môn hóa dự án rõ ràng:

  • KV cache & tái sử dụng prefix — lỗi HiCache hybrid-GDN của SGLang (#45400) và kế toán cache-hit của LiteLLM (#39057) cho thấy tái sử dụng KV giờ là một bề mặt tính đúng đắn, không chỉ là đòn bẩy hiệu năng. Nixl lease-expiry của vLLM (#61229) là ví dụ sắc nét nhất.
  • Lượng tử hóa & kernel low-bit — llama.cpp (GGML_TYPE_BF16X ở 11.5 bpw, --act-type f16, OpenCL q2_k), vLLM (Humming > Machete trên SM90, MXFP4 MoE), và Ollama (nvfp4 prefill) đều đang đua trên các đường low-bit. Toán sai âm thầm (SGLang flashinfer_mxfp4 → GPT-OSS SwiGLU, #45755) là mối nguy đang nổi lên.
  • Serving phân tán — DeepSeek-V4.1 PP tùy ý (vLLM #63106), ROCm TP MoE down-projection (#63263), SYCL tensor-parallel +19% (llama.cpp #30956), GGUF đa node qua RPC (Unsloth #13726). Lợi ích kiểu định luật Moore giờ đến từ topology, không phải kernel đơn-GPU.
  • CUDA graphs & replay — vLLM decoder replay (#63155), SGLang DSv4.1 prefill replay >16K (#45941), teardown graph diffusion của Unsloth (#14867). Graph capture là mục tiêu tối ưu mặc định; lỗi khi capture là lớp bug mới hàng đầu.
  • Attention cấp kernel — PrimTS trên Blackwell (vLLM), FA4 crash trên SM120 (SGLang), loại bỏ kq_mask tiết kiệm ~2 GB (llama.cpp). Kernel attention vẫn là khu vực đòn bẩy cao nhất, rủi ro cao nhất.

Diffusion/video cũng nổi lên như một làn hiệu năng riêng biệt (SGLang loại bỏ host-sync, Unsloth allocator flush), báo hiệu khối lượng serving multimodal đã đủ lớn để cần track tối ưu riêng.

5. Định vị Tầng

Sáu dự án chiếm bốn tầng riêng biệt, với sự chồng lấp đáng kể đang xuất hiện:

  • Serving engine (vLLM, SGLang) — Thông lượng cao, đa GPU, P/D phân tách, endpoint LLM production. Cả hai nhắm tới API tương thích OpenAI cùng các bề mặt phân tách nâng cao. vLLM nghiêng về độ rộng phần cứng và thử nghiệm frontend Rust; SGLang nghiêng về diffusion/multimodal và tương đương AMD.
  • Runtime cục bộ (llama.cpp, Ollama) — Đơn node, tập trung GGUF/MLX, phần cứng rộng (SYCL, Vulkan, Metal, ROCm, CPU). llama.cpp là phòng thí nghiệm kernel/backend; Ollama là lớp bọc sản phẩm hóa với tầng cloud. Cả hai giờ đều cung cấp realtime audio, rerank, và structured output — lấn sân serving engine.
  • Gateway (LiteLLM) — Định tuyến đa nhà cung cấp, xác thực, theo dõi chi tiêu, dịch Claude Code/Anthropic. Nằm trước mọi thứ khác; tình trạng ổn định và bảo mật của nó trực tiếp chi phối phần còn lại của ngăn xếp.
  • Huấn luyện/fine-tuning (Unsloth) — LoRA/full finetune, xuất lượng tử hóa, và giờ là bề mặt pipeline/soạn tác nhân hoàn chỉnh (Flows). Ngày càng chồng lấp với tầng gateway và serving khi Studio trở thành nền tảng tự host.

Cảnh báo chồng lấp: serving engine đang thêm tính năng kiểu gateway (structured output, định tuyến, API render/generate), gateway đang thêm dịch thuật tiến gần đến ngữ nghĩa engine, và Unsloth đang thêm điều phối workflow. Ranh giới tích hợp đang mờ đi — dự kiến sẽ có thêm ma sát tại các đường nối này.

6. Tín hiệu Xu hướng

  1. Tính đúng đắn âm thầm là biên giới độ tin cậy mới. Ba trong số các bug nghiêm trọng nhất hôm nay (vLLM #61160 rò rỉ KV liên request, SGLang #45755 kích hoạt sai, LiteLLM #34217 cache xác thực cũ) đều thất bại âm thầm — không crash, không log, chỉ có câu trả lời sai. Nhà phát triển ứng dụng phải dự trù cho kiểm tra đầu ra và canary testing, không chỉ giám sát uptime.
  2. Chuỗi cung ứng giờ là rủi ro hạ tầng hạng nhất. LiteLLM 1.107.0 (cook.pth stealer + sitecustomize RCE) và cụm Go/CVE đang diễn ra của Ollama cho thấy vệ sinh phụ thuộc là mối quan tâm hàng đầu. Pin, audit, và xác minh root CA — khoảng trống backport (#47904) nghĩa là ngay cả các image 1.106.x "an toàn" cũng mang rủi ro còn sót lại.
  3. Phân tầng phần cứng đang cứng lại, không mềm đi. Blackwell/SM120/GB300 được ưu ái ngày-0; Ampere và Intel SYCL nhận bug tính đúng đắn và nợ hiệu năng. Các đội trên phần cứng không tiên phong nên lập kế hoạch quanh độ trễ, không phải tương đương.
  4. Khối lượng công việc tác nhân đang phơi bày bug parser thất bại mềm. Rơi tool-call của GLM (SGLang #45953, #42110), rơi tool âm thầm của Ollama (#19187), khoảng trống dịch Claude Code của LiteLLM (#26224) — vòng lặp tác nhân mong manh theo cách không lộ ra trong benchmark chat. Kiểm thử tool-calling đầu-cuối theo từng backend.
  5. Serving multimodal + diffusion đang tốt nghiệp từ demo lên làn production. SANA-Sprint, MiniMax-H3 FP8 VAE, LTX-2 CFG sharding, MOSS-Image, MiniCPM-OCR — đủ hoạt động song song để cần lập kế hoạch dung lượng GPU riêng.
  6. Bề mặt workflow/soạn tác là chiến trường mới. Unsloth Flows, pipeline diffusion của SGLang, và API render/generate phân tách của vLLM đều đẩy các dự án này lên cao hơn trong ngăn xếp. Nhà phát triển tác nhân nên theo dõi hội tụ — cùng một ứng dụng có thể sớm nhắm tới cả ba.

Điều cần theo dõi tiếp: liệu vLLM/SGLang có thu hẹp khoảng cách Ampere trên DeepSeek-V4.x (hỗ trợ SM8x), liệu LiteLLM có phát hành bản backport 1.106.3 sạch, và liệu có dự án nào phát hành bộ kiểm thử tính đúng đắn có thể xác minh cho tái sử dụng KV-cache — bề mặt thất bại âm thầm lớn nhất của ngành hiện nay.

Xếp theo mức độ nghiêm trọng:

  1. CAO — SYCL F16 xuất NaN trên Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M dense sau khi sắp xếp lại mã IQ3 (#30907); cách xử lý tạm: tắt fused GEMM. Chưa có PR sửa lỗi. (#30892)
  2. CAO — CUDA/HIP Flash Attention rác ở ngữ cảnh dài trên RDNA4 (gfx1201), head_dim 256 — EOS xuất hiện ngay lập tức do logits prefill bị hỏng (#30884)
  3. CAO — Metal abort ở MUL_MAT với BF16 src1 tại K≥64, batch>8 — không có kernel BF16 mul_mm (#30973)
  4. CAO — Thông lượng decode Qwen3.8-27B sụp đổ ~25× vượt ngữ cảnh ~80K trên hybrid Gated DeltaNet, xử lý prompt không bị ảnh hưởng (#27623)
  5. TRUNG BÌNH — DeltaNet SYCL token soup trên prompt dài (Qwen3.6/3.8, Nemotron) — nhiều báo cáo trùng lặp (#29183, #29167)
  6. TRUNG BÌNH — Qwen3.8 DFlash/MTP phát ra token id ngoài biên (== n_vocab) trên Vulkan (#28158)

  8. THẤP — Thoái hóa đầu ra --tensor-split trên MoE ngữ cảnh dài, tái hiện được qua API thô (#28185)

Cũng đáng lưu ý: một vấn đề bảo mật vẫn đang mở — instruction injection qua tham số ?q= của WebUI (#25790).

6. Điều này có ý nghĩa gì với nhà phát triển ứng dụng

  • API realtime audio và rerank đang ổn định dần. Nếu bạn đang xây dựng voice agent, hãy nâng cấp lên b11828+ — sự kiện complete giờ chờ đúng lúc audio đã cam kết được xả hết, sửa lỗi race condition trong pipeline streaming. Các bên dùng rerank gửi typed content nên xem lại #29625.
  • Các mô hình hybrid-attention ngữ cảnh dài (Qwen3.8, Nemotron) hiện khá rủi ro khi chạy production. Nhiều báo cáo độc lập về sụp đổ thông lượng và token soup trên các đường SYCL, Vulkan và RDNA4. Nếu bạn phục vụ các mô hình này ở ngữ cảnh >80K, hãy ghim vào bản build đã biết là tốt và kiểm tra theo từng backend trước khi triển khai.
  • Phục vụ MoE trên VRAM hạn chế sắp được cải thiện đáng kể. Các PR expert cache cư trú trên GPU (#27861, #30966) cùng QSA không mask (#30965) nhắm trực tiếp vào nút cổ chai băng thông RAM host vốn chi phối decode với -ncmoe/-ot exps=CPU.
  • Theo dõi --act-type f16 và BF16X cho các triển khai bị giới hạn bộ nhớ. Cả hai đều giảm áp lực lên đường dữ liệu đối với các accelerator mà giới hạn là băng thông chứ không phải FLOPs.
  • Người dùng Intel SYCL nhận được thắng lợi lớn nhất trong ngày hôm nay (+19% prompt eval, tensor-parallel), nhưng cũng gánh nhiều lỗi tính đúng đắn đang mở nhất — hồi quy F16 NaN là rào cản đối với các mô hình dense Q4_K_M.
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Điểm nổi bật hôm nay

Không có bản phát hành mới trong 24 giờ qua, nhưng tốc độ PR rất cao: MLX có thêm YaRN RoPE scaling cho Qwen3/Qwen3.5 và hỗ trợ Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B với LiLiCorr speculative decoding. Về mặt ổn định, sự cố Pro cloud (#15453, 55 bình luận, 22 👍) vẫn tiếp tục chiếm sóng, cùng với hai báo cáo riêng biệt về connection-reset trên Windows (#19113, #19139) và một regression prompt-cache trên Vulkan/AMD (#19201) vẫn đang mở.

2. Bản phát hành & thay đổi breaking

Không có bản phát hành nào trong 24 giờ qua. Hai lưu ý ở tầng API cho bên tích hợp:

  • OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH không được phản ánh trong /api/show hoặc /api/tags — server báo cáo context window gốc của model, không phải giá trị bị giới hạn thực tế, nên client tính toán prompt từ metadata sẽ vượt quá. #18995
  • typical_p đã bị xóa khỏi Python API — các request giờ trả về HTTP 400. #18480

3. Hỗ trợ model & phần cứng mới

  • Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (MLX) — cấu hình expert theo từng lớp, import affine prequantized 3-bit với metadata theo module, xếp chồng expert mixed-precision, và LiLiCorr speculative decoding thông qua DFlash runner. #19229
  • YaRN scaling trong MLX cho Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 — tôn trọng metadata RoPE scaling tường minh (tần số YaRN + biên độ) trên cả text và mRoPE; bổ sung các fixture prefill/decode/partial-rotation. #19231
  • GA Gradium Phonon checkpoints — thay thế đường dẫn prerelease; đặt mức tối thiểu 0.40.9 cho hỗ trợ speech. #19227
  • GB10 (DGX Spark / Ascent GX10) được thêm vào danh sách thiết bị hỗ trợ. #13987
  • Metadata catalog cloud (context length, mức thinking, capabilities) giờ được truyền tới tất cả các harness của ollama launch. #19223

4. Hiệu năng & tối ưu hóa

  • Vulkan/AMD RADV chậm sinh token ~30× sau request đầu tiên khi bật prompt cache — thông lượng sụt 29.7× ở request thứ hai giống hệt, Mesa RADV + RX 6600 XT, Ollama 0.40.8. Đây là regression, không phải vấn đề tuning. #19201
  • Speculative decode kiểu dspark được yêu cầu để tăng tốc sinh token, lấy memtp làm tham chiếu. #17016
  • num_predict == -2 được đề xuất để lấp đầy context buffer động thay vì dùng cap tĩnh. #9547

5. Ổn định & regression

Xếp theo mức độ nghiêm trọng:

  1. Tỷ lệ thất bại 95% trên Ollama Cloud Pro với các model cloud glm-5.1, kimi-k2.5, qwen3.5, deepseek-v3.2 — dịch vụ gần như không dùng được đối với khách hàng trả phí kể từ tháng 4. #15453
  2. glm-5.3-flash:cloud bị thoái hóa — 5–8% request thất bại với hiện tượng thoái hóa token nghiêm trọng từ 2026-10-12; có báo cáo về vùng dữ liệu bị zero ở phía host. #18980
  3. Windows bị reset kết nối sau ~15s với prompt lớn (0.40.4, RTX 3090, /api/chat) — tái hiện được bất kể dùng Ollama API hay llama-server trực tiếp, nghĩa là lỗi nằm dưới gateway. #19139 · #19113
  4. Panic Maximum threads trên MLX 0.40.0 — mlx runner failed: panic: mlx: Maximum threads per threadgroup is 896 but requested 1024. Hạ cấp xuống 0.35.1 sẽ hết. #18846
  5. MLX nvfp4 prefill bị treo — request đã được nhận bị treo ở processed=total-1 dưới tải single-slot liên tục; chỉ thoát được bằng SIGTERM. #18505
  6. Assert GGML với rnj-1 — lỗi hparams.is_swa_any() khi load sau khi nâng cấp lên 0.3x. #18924
  7. Race condition khi eviction — eviction đang chờ bị hủy bởi một request keep_alive trên model đang cư trú; request đang đợi bị treo suốt cửa sổ keep-alive. #19182
  8. Tool-call bị rơi im lặng — tool được gọi theo tên không có trong tools của request sẽ trả về response rỗng với eval_count > 0. Các PR fix đang trên đường: #19228 (Qwen3 Coder XML escaping), #19226 (Gemma4 khôi phục trailing-noise), #19187
  9. CVE trong Go toolchain — 1 critical + 11 high trong các binary phát hành; cần nâng lên Go 1.26.9+. #19162 · #16033
  10. Server khởi động thất bại im lặng trên Windows Desktop 0.33.1 — server.log rỗng, không có listener; chạy ollama serve thủ công thì được. #18061; lỗi nuốt exception giờ đang được log bởi #19179

Các fix về tính đúng đắn/hành vi đã land hoặc đang chờ: giữ nguyên role system/developer cho client API trực tiếp #19199, SYSTEM "" rỗng tường minh giờ xóa thay vì kế thừa #18990, giữ lại tin nhắn cuối của user khi cắt context #19058, lỗi stream Responses giờ phát response.failed thay vì EOF #19225, và tái sử dụng thinking-settings cho Anthropic web-search #19098.

6. Điều này có ý nghĩa gì với nhà phát triển ứng dụng

  • Đừng tin /api/tags hay /api/show để tính context budget. Cứ giả định là context gốc, rồi tự giới hạn phía client. Nếu bạn dựa vào metadata để cắt, bạn sẽ vượt quá cửa sổ thực tế.
  • Windows + prompt lớn hiện không an toàn. Nếu có luồng inference trên Windows, hãy giới hạn kích thước prompt, thêm retry-with-backoff khi bị reset, hoặc pin về phiên bản đã biết là tốt cho đến khi #19139/#19113 được giải quyết.
  • Pin phiên bản một cách có chủ đích. 0.40.0 có panic MLX (#18846); 0.40.8 có regression prompt-cache AMD RADV (#19201). Với fleet hỗn hợp, hãy giữ ma trận phiên bản theo từng backend thay vì một mức sàn chung.
  • Độ bền tool-calling đang cải thiện nhanh. Các parser Qwen3 Coder, Gemma4 và Responses-stream đều có fix đang trên đường. Nếu agent của bạn bị lặp vì output tool sai định dạng, hãy theo dõi các PR này trước khi tự build workaround.
  • Người dùng Cloud Pro: báo cáo thất bại 95% đã mở từ tháng 4 mà chưa có giải pháp; hãy coi cloud là best-effort cho traffic production và luôn giữ đường fallback local.
  • Nâng cấp binary Go nếu bạn ship Ollama trong container; cụm CVE được fix bằng Go 1.26.9+ và rebuild downstream.

4. Hiệu năng & Tối ưu hóa

  • Event-loop proxy bị treo / RSS phình to khi upstream trả error body lớn — Proxy đọc error-response body không giới hạn (đã quan sát thấy HTTP 400 ~114 MB), chạy regex masking trên toàn bộ payload và truyền tiếp, làm treo event loop. Cần giới hạn kích thước. #34031
  • Latency-based routing thoái hóa thành chọn ngẫu nhiên — Race condition lost-update trong async_log_success_event khiến latency-based routing suy giảm thành chọn ngẫu nhiên có trọng số theo số deployment khi có concurrency (đề cập 16 key Anthropic + 4 key OpenAI mỗi group). #24720
  • Router bỏ qua Retry-After với group nhiều deployment — Router._time_to_sleep_before_retry chỉ tôn trọng Retry-After khi model group có một deployment duy nhất; group nhiều deployment retry ngay lập tức vào upstream dùng chung đang bị rate-limit. #34399
  • Sửa least-busy routing (PR, đã đóng/lâu ngày) — So sánh strictly less-than khiến toàn bộ traffic dồn vào deployment đầu tiên khi số in-flight bằng nhau; đã chuyển sang xử lý tie đúng. #23924

  • Routing nhiều deployment không đảm bảo công bằng: latency-based routing sụp đổ dưới concurrency (#24720), và Retry-After bị bỏ qua với group nhiều deployment (#34399). Thêm client-side backoff và tránh fan-out vào upstream dùng chung duy nhất.
  • Nếu bạn build trên Claude Code / Anthropic /v1/messages: một số lỗ hổng translation ảnh hưởng đến streaming tool call (#25390), adaptive thinking (#26224), và Bedrock web-search interception (#26252). Test trên đúng backend của bạn trước khi phụ thuộc vào các đường này.
  • Postgres là dependency cứng ở quy mô lớn: cạn connection và DB chập chờn có thể làm sập toàn bộ xác thực key (#34479, #26237). Cân nhắc local auth cache với invalidation đúng (lưu ý lỗ rò cache team-delete hiện có, #34217) và dự phòng connection-pool.
  • Phòng chống error body upstream quá lớn (#34031) — giảm timeout/
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Điểm nổi bật hôm nay

Không có bản phát hành mới trong 24h qua, nhưng hàng đợi PR cực kỳ sôi động: loạt trình chỉnh sửa node Flows (#14730, #14889, #14891, #14898, #14899, #14904, #14905) đang được hợp nhất theo dạng xếp chồng, mở rộng Studio thành một bề mặt soạn thảo pipeline/game/agent hoàn chỉnh. Về phía hạ tầng, phục vụ GGUF đa node qua llama.cpp RPC tiếp tục trưởng thành (#13726, #14274, #10323, #10280), và một loạt bản sửa lỗi ổn định đã được hợp nhất cho xử lý đồ thị CUDA diffusion (#14867, #14777) và staging LoRA ảnh cho sd-server (#14860). Các regression mới đáng chú ý nhất được báo cáo hôm nay liên quan đến việc âm thầm fallback về CPU trên AMD RDNA3 Linux (#14906) và đường phục hồi MacOS Metal OOM (#14431).

2. Phát hành & Thay đổi phá vỡ tương thích

Không có. Không có bản phát hành nào trong 24h qua; không có mục di chuyển API/config.

3. Hỗ trợ Model & Phần cứng mới

  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (GGUF) lỗi tải — người dùng báo cáo kiến trúc deepseek41-dspark không được llama.cpp đi kèm nhận diện; việc xử lý sidecar DSpark/DFlash đang được giải quyết trong #14431, nơi dành riêng bộ nhớ sidecar trong --fit-target và thêm phục hồi Metal OOM. Issue: #14695.
  • MOSS-Image port trong cây — bản dựng lượng tử hóa và GGUF qua stable-diffusion.cpp, được thêm như một họ ảnh trong Studio (#14552, hiện đã đóng/đã hợp nhất).
  • Phục vụ GGUF đa node — chia N-node qua nhiều máy qua llama.cpp RPC, xếp chồng trên orchestrator hai-Spark (#13726); ghép nối mạng gia đình với mutual TLS (#14274); bộ gợi ý topology hai-Spark với async replica router (#10323); clustering DGX Spark một/hai node và huấn luyện pipeline (#10280).
  • Qwen3.5 GatedDeltaNet — context parallel / FSDP2 sharding cho các lớp hồi quy hybrid vẫn chưa được hỗ trợ; issue đã đóng mà không ghi nhận bản sửa (#12051).
  • OmniVoice — yêu cầu hỗ trợ finetune full/LoRA và inference trong Studio (#14660).
  • Giới hạn bộ nhớ XPU/MPS — khoảng trống còn lại về giới hạn bộ nhớ GPU cho huấn luyện XPU và MPS, cùng việc sinh ảnh tuân thủ ngân sách VRAM (#8178).

4. Hiệu năng & Tối ưu hóa

  • Sửa lỗi flush allocator diffusion — pre-hook mã hóa prompt gọi torch.cuda.empty_cache() sau mỗi lần giải phóng nhóm trên các tầng offload/streaming, gây đồng bộ thiết bị cộng với churn allocator trên mỗi prompt. Bản sửa dừng flush mỗi lần mã hóa (#14777, đã đóng).
  • Tháo dỡ đồ thị CUDA diffusion — dừng ghi đồ thị CUDA một khi VMM arena đã thất bại, và tách nó ra, tránh việc ghi đồ thị lãng phí dưới low_vram CPU offload (#14867, đã đóng).
  • KV preemption cho chat song song — một llama-server giữ một KV cache duy nhất giờ đây tạm dừng/preempt công việc qua --preempt-ram khi được hỗ trợ, với Studio chuyển giao preemption cho server; nhắm đến đồng thời tốt hơn trên cache chia sẻ (#10301, đang mở).
  • pre-commit.ci compute — scripts/enforce_kwargs_spacing.py cực kỳ chậm và tạo tải CI đáng kể trên repo có lượng PR cao (#14174, đã đóng).
  • Embedding lưu trữ hội thoại bị đình trệ — các cuộc trò chuyện dài, nhiều công cụ có thể mất hàng phút trong embedding lưu trữ dựa trên CPU trước khi llama.cpp nhận được bất kỳ yêu cầu inference nào trên Studio Desktop v0.1.909-beta (#14519, đang mở).

5. Ổn định & Regression

Xếp hạng theo mức độ nghiêm trọng:

  1. Âm thầm fallback về CPU trên Linux AMD native (RDNA3/gfx1100) — Studio thêm /opt/rocm/lib vào đầu khiến GPU bị ẩn khỏi llama-server đi kèm; nghi ngờ là regression từ bản sửa #7208. Cài lại AppImage mới trên CachyOS vẫn tái hiện (#14906, đang mở, chưa có PR sửa).
  2. MacOS Metal OOM khiến llama-server lỗi vĩnh viễn — prefill đầu tiên chết với kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory, sau đó mọi yêu cầu đều thất bại; đường phục hồi trong #14431 (đang mở).
  3. Tệp đính kèm trở nên không thể đọc vĩnh viễn sau tự động nén — ảnh/PDF bị mất sau nén, và search_conversation không bao giờ được gọi (#14708, đang mở).
  4. Mất đồng bộ model cục bộ đa tài khoản — nhiều tài khoản LAN trên cùng một inference server mất đồng bộ tải model (#12365, đã đóng).
  5. Lỗi linker inference LoRA Intel XPU trên Windows — tham số linker GNU và MSVC bị trộn lẫn (#14807, đang mở).
  6. Lemonade/FastFlowLM chat+models ngừng hoạt động — regression trên AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 sau cơ chế #11743 (#14650, đang mở).
  7. Regression UI/UX — xử lý phím mũi tên trong chat MacOS (#14764), bảng trình duyệt mất bản xem trước đã render khi chỉnh sửa yêu cầu (#14783), chọn model không lưu lại qua các cuộc trò chuyện đa model (#14506, đã đóng), tin nhắn assistant không thể chỉnh sửa (#13938, đã đóng).
  8. Lỗi xuất — model có mã từ xa không thể xuất từ UI (#14688, đang mở).
  9. Vệ sinh chuỗi cung ứng — trình cài đặt ghim uv ≥0.13.4 (loại bỏ root CA emSign) trong #14894.

6. Điều này có nghĩa gì với nhà phát triển ứng dụng

  • Studio đang trở thành một nền tảng, không chỉ là trình huấn luyện. Ngăn xếp Flows (#14730 + các phần tiếp theo) thêm trình chỉnh sửa node, sub-flows, chế độ xem ứng dụng, polling job, GPU lease, khối memory-stream (mẫu Generative Agents), và khối chuyển đổi dữ liệu/tài liệu. Nếu bạn xây dựng pipeline agentic, hãy theo dõi bề mặt này — nó giờ chồng lấn với các workflow kiểu Langflow/Flowise/n8n và được thiết kế cho thực thi model cục bộ.
  • Triển khai đa người dùng / đa tenant cần cẩn thận. Mất đồng bộ đa tài khoản LAN (#12365) và yêu cầu lời chào/cấu hình theo người dùng (#14680) cho thấy Studio đang được dùng như một inference server chia sẻ. Hãy dự kiến các cạnh chưa mượt quanh cách ly phiên và trạng thái model cho đến khi chúng được hợp nhất.
  • Người dùng AMD/Linux và Windows-Intel nên ghim đường dẫn ROCm/oneAPI đã biết là tốt — hành vi thêm vào đầu (#14906) có thể âm thầm đẩy bạn xuống CPU, đây là một vực thẳm về độ trễ, không phải một vụ crash.
  • Khối lượng công việc agent ngữ cảnh dài có chi phí trước inference ẩn trên Studio Desktop: embedding lưu trữ trước khi llama.cpp nhận yêu cầu (#14519). Hãy dự trù cho nó hoặc tắt lưu trữ trong các vòng lặp nhạy cảm độ trễ.
  • Lên kế hoạch cho tranh chấp KV cache nếu bạn ghép nhiều chat vào một server; công việc preemption (#10301) là hướng đi nhưng chưa được hợp nhất.
  • Phục vụ đa node qua RPC là thật nhưng còn tiên phong — ghép nối mutual-TLS (#14274) và chọn topology (#10323) là tùy chọn và nhắm đến thiết lập home-lab/DGX Spark; đừng chuẩn hóa nó cho production vội.

Bản tin này được tạo tự động bởi agents-radar tự động tạo.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-10-23

Generated: 2026-10-23 04:29 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project AI Infrastructure Report — 2026-10-23

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI infrastructure stack is in a correctness-over-features phase: across all six projects, high-severity stability regressions (silent KV contamination, supply-chain compromise, wrong-activation kernels) dominate the tracker relative to new model announcements. Frontier model support has consolidated around a small set of architectures — DeepSeek-V4.x, Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.x, Nemotron 3.5 — and the competitive race is now about day-0 checkpoint coverage per hardware tier rather than net-new model classes. Hardware diversification is real but uneven: NVIDIA Blackwell/SM120/GB300 and AMD ROCm/MI355X dominate perf work, while Ampere (SM8x) and Intel SYCL are increasingly second-class citizens on the newest checkpoints. On the gateway and training layers, the story is risk management — LiteLLM's 1.107.0 supply-chain event and Ollama Cloud Pro's long-running outage are reminders that the "boring" middle of the stack carries outsized blast radius. Meanwhile, workflow/agent-authoring surfaces (Unsloth Flows, SGLang diffusion, llama.cpp realtime audio) are expanding, pushing serving engines into application-platform territory.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Open Issues Highlighted PRs Highlighted Release Status (24h) Dominant Signal
vLLM Serving engine ~7 (incl. 2 silent-corruption) ~10+ None DSv4.1 graph capture + PD-KV correctness
SGLang Serving engine ~10 (incl. scheduler crash) ~8 None GLM/Kimi correctness + diffusion host-sync
llama.cpp Local runtime ~8 ~10 7 releases (b11815–b11829) SYCL perf + long-context bugs
Ollama Local runtime + cloud ~10 ~5 None Cloud outage + Windows regressions
LiteLLM Gateway ~20+ ~10 None (yank, no release) Supply-chain compromise
Unsloth Fine-tuning platform ~9 ~7 None Flows node editor + multi-node GGUF

Note: counts reflect digest-highlighted items only, not exhaustive trackers. llama.cpp is the only project with a shipping release cadence; LiteLLM's "no release" is a yank, not a quiet day.

3. Model Support Race

Frontier model coverage is converging, but hardware-tier coverage diverges sharply.

Model / Arch vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama Unsloth
DeepSeek-V4.1 / V4-Flash ✅ (SM100 first; SM8x pending #50576) ✅ (ROCm prefill CP #43465) ⚠️ DSv4.1-Flash-1017 load fail #14695 ❌ ⚠️ sidecar fix #14431
Kimi-K3 — ✅ (with caveats: GB300 #45367, SM90 #45755) — ❌ ❌
GLM-5.3-Flash / GLM5 — ✅ (SM90 perf #45373, SM120 #42012) ✅ (GLM5 input opts) ⚠️ cloud degeneration #18980 ❌
Qwen3.8 / Qwen4exp ✅ (ROCm MI355X) — ✅ (DFlash, kq_mask elim #30965) ✅ (cloud only) ❌
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt — — ✅ (GQA/tokenizer #23343) ✅ (MLX 74B-A9B #19229) ❌
MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 / MOSS-Image — ✅ SANA-Sprint ✅ MiniCPM-OCR ❌ ✅ MOSS-Image
Muse Spark ✅ (ROCm MoE #63263) ✅ (Day-0 #44664–67) ❌ ❌ ❌

Who's ahead: vLLM and SGLang are the day-0 frontier engines, but both gate the newest DeepSeek checkpoints behind SM90+/Blackwell — leaving A100/A800 and consumer Ampere out. llama.cpp has the broadest breadth of model support (Nemotron, GLM5, MiniCPM, MOSS) but trails on the very newest DeepSeek family. Ollama leads on turnkey MLX/Nemotron packaging for Mac and DGX Spark. Unsloth is the outlier: focused on multimodal + GGUF + multi-node rather than raw frontier LLM coverage.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort is concentrated in five clusters, with clear project specialization:

  • KV cache & prefix reuse — SGLang's HiCache hybrid-GDN bug (#45400) and LiteLLM's cache-hit accounting (#39057) show KV reuse is now a correctness surface, not just a perf lever. vLLM's Nixl lease-expiry (#61229) is the sharpest example.
  • Quantization & low-bit kernels — llama.cpp (GGML_TYPE_BF16X at 11.5 bpw, --act-type f16, OpenCL q2_k), vLLM (Humming > Machete on SM90, MXFP4 MoE), and Ollama (nvfp4 prefill) are all racing on low-bit paths. Silent wrong-math (SGLang flashinfer_mxfp4 → GPT-OSS SwiGLU, #45755) is the emerging hazard.
  • Distributed serving — DeepSeek-V4.1 arbitrary PP (vLLM #63106), ROCm TP MoE down-projection (#63263), SYCL tensor-parallel +19% (llama.cpp #30956), multi-node GGUF over RPC (Unsloth #13726). Moore's-law-style gains now come from topology, not single-GPU kernels.
  • CUDA graphs & replay — vLLM decoder replay (#63155), SGLang DSv4.1 >16K prefill replay (#45941), Unsloth diffusion graph teardown (#14867). Graph capture is the default optimization target; failures under capture are the top new bug class.
  • Kernel-level attention — PrimTS on Blackwell (vLLM), FA4 crashes on SM120 (SGLang), kq_mask elimination saving ~2 GB (llama.cpp). Attention kernels remain the highest-leverage, highest-risk area.

Diffusion/video also emerged as a distinct perf lane (SGLang host-sync elimination, Unsloth allocator flush), signaling the multimodal serving workload is now large enough to warrant its own optimization track.

5. Layer Positioning

The six projects occupy four distinct layers, with meaningful overlap emerging:

  • Serving engines (vLLM, SGLang) — High-throughput, multi-GPU, disaggregated P/D, production LLM endpoints. Both target OpenAI-compatible APIs plus advanced disaggregated surfaces. vLLM leans toward hardware breadth and Rust-frontend experimentation; SGLang leans toward diffusion/multimodal and AMD parity.
  • Local runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama) — Single-node, GGUF/MLX-centric, broad hardware (SYCL, Vulkan, Metal, ROCm, CPU). llama.cpp is the kernel/backend lab; Ollama is the productized wrapper with a cloud tier. Both now offer realtime audio, rerank, and structured output — encroaching on serving-engine territory.
  • Gateway (LiteLLM) — Cross-provider routing, auth, spend tracking, Claude Code/Anthropic translation. Sits in front of everything else; its reliability and security posture directly gate the rest of the stack.
  • Training/fine-tuning (Unsloth) — LoRA/full finetune, quantization export, and now a full pipeline/agent-authoring surface (Flows). Increasingly overlaps with gateway and serving layers as Studio becomes a self-hosted platform.

Overlap warning: serving engines are adding gateway-like features (structured output, routing, render/generate APIs), gateway is adding translation that edges toward engine semantics, and Unsloth is adding workflow orchestration. Integration boundaries are blurring — expect more friction at these seams.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Silent correctness is the new reliability frontier. Three of today's most severe bugs (vLLM #61160 cross-request KV leak, SGLang #45755 wrong activation, LiteLLM #34217 stale auth cache) fail silently — no crash, no log, just wrong answers. Application developers must budget for output-validation and canary testing, not just uptime monitoring.
  2. The supply chain is now a first-class infra risk. LiteLLM 1.107.0 (cook.pth stealer + sitecustomize RCE) and the ongoing Ollama Go/CVE cluster show dependency hygiene is a top-tier concern. Pin, audit, and verify root CAs — the backport gap (#47904) means even "safe" 1.106.x images carry residual risk.
  3. Hardware tiering is hardening, not softening. Blackwell/SM120/GB300 get day-0 love; Ampere and Intel SYCL get correctness bugs and perf debt. Teams on non-frontier hardware should plan around lag, not parity.
  4. Agent workloads are exposing soft-fail parser bugs. GLM tool-call drops (SGLang #45953, #42110), Ollama silent tool drops (#19187), LiteLLM Claude Code translation gaps (#26224) — agent loops are brittle in ways that don't surface in chat benchmarks. Test tool-calling end-to-end per backend.
  5. Multimodal + diffusion serving is graduating from demo to production lane. SANA-Sprint, MiniMax-H3 FP8 VAE, LTX-2 CFG sharding, MOSS-Image, MiniCPM-OCR — enough parallel activity to warrant dedicated GPU capacity planning.
  6. Workflow/authoring surfaces are the new battleground. Unsloth Flows, SGLang diffusion pipelines, and vLLM's disaggregated render/generate APIs all push these projects up the stack. Agent developers should watch for convergence — the same app may soon target all three.

What to watch next: whether vLLM/SGLang close the Ampere gap on DeepSeek-V4.x (SM8x support), whether LiteLLM ships a clean 1.106.3 backport, and whether any project ships a verifiable correctness test harness for KV-cache reuse — the industry's largest silent-failure surface today.

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24h, but issue and PR activity remains intense across three fronts: DeepSeek-V4.1 (DSv4.1) graph capture and pipeline-parallel work (PRs #63264, #63155, #63106), a cluster of correctness bugs around disaggregated prefill/decode KV reuse (#61229, #61160), and a batch of ROCm/MI355X performance optimizations for quantized MoE models (#63263, #57149, #59575). The Rust frontend continues its march toward feature parity (#44280) with a dependency rebase onto llm-multimodal v1.14 (#59854).

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None in the last 24h. Note that several open PRs touch parameter lifecycle semantics under process_weights_after_loading (e.g., #62407), which may affect custom quantized model implementations once merged.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • SM8x support for DeepSeek-V4-Flash — Feature request (118 comments, the most-discussed issue today) to enable Ampere A100/A800 and RTX 30xx support for DeepSeek-V4-Flash / -0731 checkpoints, which currently only run on newer arches.
  • PrimTS attention for Step5 on Blackwell — Opt-in PrimTS DSA and sliding-window attention for SM100/103/107, BF16 and E4M3 QKV; requires an upstream FlashInfer patch.
  • Arbitrary PP partitions for DeepSeek-V4.1 — Removes the restriction that a pipeline cut cannot fall inside a KV-sharing layer group.
  • Rust frontend rebased to llm-multimodal v1.14 — Keeps the Rust path current with the multimodal crate; still gated behind VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • DSv4.1 prefill index sentinels — Replaces a full sparse-index workspace memset with -1 sentinel writes from the combine kernel, removing one CUDA launch and a full-row write per prefill layer.
  • DSv4.1 decoder replay graph capture — Captures replay graphs on the model graphs' stream to reuse the shared graph pool; targets GB200 prefill.
  • ROCm/TP MoE down-projection for Muse Spark — Column-shards the MXFP4 MoE down projection at TP > 1, replacing a reduce-scatter with smaller gathers for prefill batches ≥1024 tokens.
  • Humming before Machete on SM90 — 4-bit weight-only linear layers (GPTQ/AWQ/compressed-tensors W4A16) now prefer Humming over Machete on Hopper.
  • ROCm MI355X trackers: #57149 (Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B) and #59575 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) continue landing stacked PRs.
  • GB10/DGX Spark weight loading — Per-tensor H2D copies from safetensors mmap views are flagged as a platform-specific cost on GB10.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. NixlConnector lease-expiry race — KV blocks released while a remote READ is in flight; decode silently consumes overwritten KV. Silent data corruption. No fix PR referenced.
  2. Cross-request KV contamination in PD disaggregation — With automatic prefix caching enabled in a NIXL P/D deployment on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, responses intermittently leak content from other requests. Reproducible; clean with --no-enable-prefix-caching.
  3. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prompt truncation on GB10 — Content beyond ~2048 tokens (indexer_budget) is invisible to the model on sm121 nightlies.
  4. HiSparse trtllm-gen out-of-bounds read — Random illegal memory access in sparse MLA prefill; fix PR pads staged KV.
  5. PP2 tool-calling garbling on ROCm — GLM-5.2-FP8 DSA with chunked prefill and PP2 produces garbled output; PP1 is fine.
  6. Qwen3.5 json_schema garbled spaces — Structured output regression persists.
  7. DeepSeek-VL2 encoder-cache collision — Fix PR open for cache identity across cropping modes.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Avoid prefix caching in NIXL P/D deployments for now. #61160 is silent, probabilistic cross-request contamination — the worst failure mode for multi-tenant serving. Until fixed, run with --no-enable-prefix-caching if you use PD disaggregation.
  • Treat lease-based KV pull flows as unsafe under load. #61229 means decode can consume stale KV without erroring; monitor for accuracy anomalies rather than crashes.
  • Ampere users are still the have-nots for the newest DeepSeek checkpoints. If you're on A100/A800, #50576 is the issue to track before planning a DeepSeek-V4-Flash rollout.
  • Disaggregated serving APIs are stabilizing. The render/generate/derender surface is getting consistent semantics across streaming and batch paths (#63148, #42729, #47161) — worth tracking if you're building on the disaggregated endpoints rather than /v1/chat/completions.
  • Rust frontend is not production-ready. #44280 explicitly labels it experimental; enable only for evaluation.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24h, but the tracker is dense with GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3 correctness work across SM90/SM120/GB300, plus a fresh high-severity scheduler crash with --enable-lmcache. On the performance side, a wave of diffusion host-sync elimination PRs (Cosmos3, Qwen-Image-2.1, LTX-2) and DeepSeek-V4 prefill/C4-indexer tuning landed in review. The long-running flaky-CI tracker continues to dominate comment volume, signaling ongoing CI infrastructure debt that may slow PR velocity.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

No new releases in the last 24h. Note one active crash affecting v0.5.22 configuration compatibility (radix cache + LM cache interaction, see §5), which users on that version should be aware of.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • GLM5 / glm5-next — input optimization landing; QSA without kq_mask in progress (#31009)
  • Hexagon (Snapdragon NPU) — SGN op (#30346) and CEIL op (#31006) added
  • OpenCL — initial q2_k quantization support (#30999)
  • New quant type GGML_TYPE_BF16X — near-lossless bfloat16 recompression at 11.5 bpw (1.39× smaller than BF16), with CPU + GPU execution (#29896)

4. Performance & Optimization

  • SYCL tensor-parallel prompt eval +19% — new ggml_sycl_comm_exchange() makes -sm tensor as fast as -sm layer, zero PPL change, on Arc Pro B70 (#30956)
  • MoE expert caching — GPU-resident LRU cache for host-offloaded expert weights (#27861); companion PR runs missed experts on CPU with a tuning script (#30966)
  • kq_mask elimination — Qwen4exp and GLM5-next QSA no longer allocate the mask, saving ~2 GB GPU/host at ub 4096 and 4 GB at ub 8192 for expert cache headroom (#30965, #31009)
  • FP16 activations (--act-type f16) — end-to-end F16 compute graph for accelerators bottlenecked on the activation data path (#31011)

Ranked by severity:

  2. HIGH — CUDA/HIP Flash Attention garbage at long context on RDNA4 (gfx1201), head_dim 256 — immediate EOS from corrupted prefill logits (#30884)

  4. HIGH — Qwen3.8-27B decode throughput collapse ~25× beyond ~80K context on hybrid Gated DeltaNet, prompt processing unaffected (#27623)

  6. MED — Qwen3.8 DFlash/MTP emits OOB token id (== n_vocab) on Vulkan (#28158)
  7. MED — Nemotron 3/3.5 GGUFs mistagged pixtral → wrong pre-tokenizer (#30894)

Also of note: a security issue remains open — instruction injection via the WebUI ?q= parameter (#25790).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Realtime audio and rerank APIs are stabilizing. If you're building voice agents, upgrade to b11828+ — the complete event now correctly waits for committed audio to drain, fixing race conditions in streaming pipelines. Rerank consumers sending typed content should review #29625.
  • Long-context hybrid-attention models (Qwen3.8, Nemotron) are risky in production right now. Multiple independent reports of throughput collapse and token soup on SYCL, Vulkan, and RDNA4 paths. If you serve these at >80K context, pin to a known-good build and validate per-backend before rollout.
  • MoE serving on constrained VRAM is about to get materially better. The GPU-resident expert cache PRs (#27861, #30966) plus mask-free QSA (#30965) directly target the host-RAM-bandwidth bottleneck that dominates -ncmoe/-ot exps=CPU decode.
  • Watch --act-type f16 and BF16X for memory-bound deployments. Both reduce data-path pressure for accelerators where bandwidth, not FLOPs, is the limit.
  • Intel SYCL users get the biggest single win today (+19% prompt eval, tensor-parallel), but also bear the most open correctness bugs — the F16 NaN regression is a blocker for Q4_K_M dense models.

No releases in the last 24h. Two API-level notes for integrators:

  • typical_p removed from the Python API — requests now return HTTP 400. #18480

  • Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (MLX) — per-layer expert configs, 3-bit prequantized affine import with per-module metadata, mixed-precision expert stacking, and LiLiCorr speculative decoding via the DFlash runner. #19229

  • GB10 (DGX Spark / Ascent GX10) added to supported devices. #13987
  • Cloud catalog metadata (context length, thinking levels, capabilities) now propagated to all ollama launch harnesses. #19223

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Vulkan/AMD RADV ~30× generation slowdown after the first request with prompt cache enabled — a 29.7× throughput collapse on second identical request, Mesa RADV + RX 6600 XT, Ollama 0.40.8. This is a regression, not a tuning issue. #19201
  • dspark-style speculative decode requested to raise generation speed, citing memtp as a reference implementation. #17016
  • num_predict == -2 proposed to fill the context buffer dynamically instead of a static cap. #9547

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Ollama Cloud Pro 95% failure rate across glm-5.1, kimi-k2.5, qwen3.5, deepseek-v3.2 cloud models — service effectively unusable for a paying customer since April. #15453
  2. glm-5.3-flash:cloud degeneration — 5–8% of requests fail with massive token degeneration since 2026-10-12; reported host-side zeroed data areas. #18980
  3. Windows connection resets ~15s into large prompts (0.40.4, RTX 3090, /api/chat) — reproducible regardless of Ollama API vs. direct llama-server, so the fault sits below the gateway. #19139 · #19113
  4. MLX 0.40.0 Maximum threads panic — mlx runner failed: panic: mlx: Maximum threads per threadgroup is 896 but requested 1024. Downgrade to 0.35.1 resolves. #18846
  5. MLX nvfp4 prefill stall — admitted request hangs at processed=total-1 under sustained single-slot load; only SIGTERM recovery. #18505
  6. rnj-1 GGML assert — hparams.is_swa_any() failure on load after 0.3x upgrade. #18924
  7. Eviction race — pending eviction cancelled by a keep_alive request on the resident model; waiting request stalls for the full keep-alive window. #19182
  8. Silent tool-call drop — tool invoked by name not in the request's tools returns empty response with eval_count > 0. Fix PRs in flight: #19228 (Qwen3 Coder XML escaping), #19226 (Gemma4 trailing-noise recovery), #19187
  9. Go toolchain CVEs — 1 critical + 11 high in released binaries; upgrade to Go 1.26.9+ required. #19162 · #16033
  10. Silent server-start failure on Windows Desktop 0.33.1 — server.log stays empty, no listener; manual ollama serve works. #18061; swallowing bug now being logged by #19179

Correctness/behavioral fixes landed or pending: system/developer role preservation for direct API clients #19199, explicit empty SYSTEM "" now clears instead of inheriting #18990, last-user-message preserved during context truncation #19058, Responses stream failures now emit response.failed instead of EOF #19225, and Anthropic web-search thinking-settings reuse #19098.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Don't trust /api/tags or /api/show for context budgeting. Assume native context, then cap client-side. If you rely on metadata to truncate, you will overshoot the effective window.
  • Windows + large prompts is currently unsafe. If you have a Windows inference path, either cap prompt size, add retry-with-backoff on resets, or pin to a known-good version until #19139/#19113 are resolved.
  • Pin versions deliberately. 0.40.0 has an MLX panic (#18846); 0.40.8 has the AMD RADV prompt-cache regression (#19201). For mixed fleets, keep a per-backend version matrix rather than a single version floor.
  • Tool-calling robustness is improving fast. The Qwen3 Coder, Gemma4, and Responses-stream parsers all have fixes in flight. If your agent loops on malformed tool output, watch these PRs before building workarounds.
  • Cloud Pro users: the 95% failure report has been open since April with no resolution; treat cloud as best-effort for production traffic and keep a local fallback path.
  • Upgrade Go binaries if you ship Ollama in a container; the CVE cluster is fixed by Go 1.26.9+ and downstream rebuilds.

The dominant story remains the supply-chain compromise of litellm 1.107.0, with PyPI and Docker latest/main-stable/main-latest tags now yanked, but a backport gap persists: the eMudhra root CA fix (#47670) is only on main, leaving all published 1.106.x images still trusting the compromised root chain.
